description_full: Tactile Systems Technology, Inc., a medical technology company, develops and provides medical devices to treat underserved chronic diseases in the United States. It offers Flexitouch Plus system, a pneumatic compression device for the treatment of lymphedema, phlebolymphedema, lipedema, venous insufficiencies, and other types of edema and leg ulcers; Entre Plus System, a pneumatic compression device for the at-home treatment of lymphedema, chronic edema, venous insufficiency, and chronic wounds. The company also provides Nimbl, a pneumatic compression platform for the treatment of upper extremity lymphedema; Kylee, a mobile application to help patients learn about lymphedema, track their symptoms, and treatment, as well as to share their progress with their doctor; and AffloVest, a portable high frequency chest wall oscillation vest to treat patients with retained pulmonary secretions resulting from bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, and various neuromuscular disorders. Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. was incorporated in 1995 and is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

financial_summary: Tactile Systems Technology, Inc is a small-cap healthcare business with a $583M market cap on $330M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 71% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $40M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.24× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 28× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield of 4.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.3% of the shares.
